summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old male with a history of quadriplegia, tracheostomy, GJ tube, and ileostomy was admitted from his nursing home for fever, tachycardia, and suspected infection. He was found to have severe sepsis with multiple possible sources, including pneumonia, bacteremia, and a deep right gluteal ulcer. Imaging revealed multifocal pneumonia and MRI-confirmed osteomyelitis of the right ischial tuberosity. Blood cultures grew coagulase-negative Staphylococcus, and sputum showed sparse Pseudomonas aeruginosa, likely colonization. He was treated with broad-spectrum antibiotics initially, then transitioned to piperacillin-tazobactam for a six-week course of osteomyelitis. Hypernatremia resolved with IV fluids, and warfarin was restarted with bridging. The family opted for a comfort-focused approach, avoiding surgical intervention. He was discharged to extended care with OPAT, stable vitals, and improving labs.
